input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore: new research-algorithm tool, survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier, log-rank, Cox PH)
errors: Swapped median-CI bounds in the first engine draft (lo/hi band keys reversed); caught by the lifelines comparison before commit.
First test draft asserted that the Breslow score test equals the log-rank test with tied times; it is exact only without ties. Replaced with an untied identity test.

First CI run went red on four registration steps a new venture needs, none in the venture's own tests: launched.json date (launched.mjs --write), sibling back-links (siblings budget 0, so the three research-tool pages now link survival-analysis), and the opt-out switch count in platform/privacy/optout-persistence.test.mjs (1306 -> 1307). All fixed in the second commit.
integrity_issues: Draft post and VENTURE.yaml claimed web calculators 'draw a curve and stop' without any survey; removed before commit. Draft PAPERS had an archive.org URL for Greenwood (1926) that was guessed; replaced with a scholar search link. DOIs could not be resolved from the session (doi.org blocked), as the README says.

doc_friction.issue: --for-changes skips the portfolio-pages 'Build the site' step (it has ${{ }} expressions), then reports the two _site checks after it as FAIL; a reader has to work out that these are artefacts and build the site by hand.
run_workflow_locally.py --for-changes on a new venture outlasts the 600 s foreground limit; the line saying to use run_in_background covers venture tests but not this command.

The 'definition of done' table for a new research tool leaves out three repo-wide registrations that CI enforces: launched.mjs --write, back-links from sibling pages (siblings.mjs orphan budget 0), and bumping SWITCHES_IN_THE_CATALOGUE in platform/privacy/optout-persistence.test.mjs. Each cost one red CI round.

notes: Idea: fourth 'research algorithms as tools' venture, survival-analysis (named as a next paper in portfolio/research-tools/README.md). The engine is written from the papers. eval/reference.py fits lifelines 0.30.3 and statsmodels 0.15.0 on the Freireich 1963 example plus three seeded tie-heavy cases. Results: Cox coefficients match statsmodels to 1e-8 (Efron and Breslow), KM to 1e-12, tests to 1e-9. lifelines differs from both at about 1e-5 because of its looser Newton stop. On the example, adding sex and logWBC flags sex in the PH check at p = 0.052. 44 node tests pass. A Playwright smoke test at 1100 and 375 px showed no console errors and no overflow. Local CI (run_workflow_locally --for-changes): 109 steps passed before the 590 s cut; the two _site failures came from the skipped build step. Real CI caught the three registrations noted in errors; after fixing them, siblings.test.mjs (20/20), launched.test.mjs, the opt-out count test and the three sibling page tests pass locally. Next: a stratified Cox model, then late entry. No agent doc was written: the venture README and research-tools README carry what the next run needs.

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
